name: San Juan Island National Historical Park
author: parks-page-legacy
summary: San Juan Island National Historical Park in Washington State preserves the sites of the 1859 Pig War confrontation between the United States and Great Britain over possession of the San Juan Islands. The dispute began when an American settler shot a British-owned pig and escalated into a military standoff with both nations deploying forces on the island. The conflict was resolved through 12 years of joint military occupation and ultimately settled by international arbitration in 1872, when Kaiser Wilhelm I of Germany ruled in favor of the United States. The park preserves both the American Camp and English Camp — the respective military installations — and the island's prairie, forest, and shoreline ecosystems. The park was established in 1966.
